Naturally then, with infla tionary cosmology strongly suggesting something totally bizarre-that 70 percent of the universe's mass/energy has yet to be measured or identified- physicists have yearned for independent confirmation. It has long been realized that measurement of the deceleration parameter would do the trick. Since just after the initial inflationary burst, ordinary attractive gravity has been slowing the expansion of space. The rate at which this slowing occurs is called the deceleration parameter. A precise measurement of the parameter would provide independent insight into the total amount of matter in the universe: more matter, whether or not it gives off light, implies a greater gravitational pull and hence a more pronounced slow ing of spatial expansion.
